claims.text: Stepwise thermo-mechanical treatment can steer phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Sequential homogenization, rolling, and staged thermal treatment promotes coherent nanoprecipitate formation.
The resulting coherent nanoprecipitates strengthen the alloy without excessively compromising ductility.
Homogenized or as-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs have a largely single-phase matrix.
The proposed route comprises high-temperature homogenization, hot and cold rolling, and subsequent staged thermal treatments.
The processing should be conducted in an inert atmosphere.
An intermediate anneal followed by lower-temperature aging is a suitable stepwise thermal sequence.
A controlled combination of hot- and cold-rolling reductions is part of the phase-control route.
The treatment will form coherent nanoprecipitates analogous to δ lamellae and γ″ particles within the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni matrix.
The coherent nanoprecipitates interact with dislocations.
The precipitates hinder dislocation motion through pinning or moderate shearing.
An optimized balance of precipitation hardening and stress relief enhances yield strength while maintaining ductility.
The stepwise-processed alloy will have significantly higher yield strength than an alloy subjected to conventional single-step aging.
The stepwise-processed alloy will have significantly higher ultimate tensile strength than an alloy subjected to conventional single-step aging.
The stepwise-processed alloy will retain or improve ductility relative to conventionally treated material.
Phase stability and nucleation kinetics in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs are sufficiently similar to those of the cited refractory HEA to permit transfer of the processing concept.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies sequential aging treatments at different temperatures, whereas the conditions and cited process describe an intermediate anneal followed by a single lower-temperature aging treatment.
